ideas.description: Explore diagnostic plus systems change, with identical math. Recent keep and discard decisions are noise-limited: E042, E045, E046 and E048 all landed between their thresholds, and the tip's seeds 0–2 mean has read 0.7532 / 0.7525 / 0.7497 / 0.7544 across four builds of the same commit. Before any further sub-0.15 pp comparison, find out whether that build-to-build spread can be removed. Run offline on the E036 tip (commit 60645dd) through the harness code path, seeds 0–2. (1) Build once, then run seeds 0–2 twice in the same process. Record whether per-seed accuracies are bit-identical, which tests for within-build nondeterminism such as cuDNN wgrad atomics. (2) Build twice in fresh processes with private inductor cache dirs, using mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' for every step variant. Compare per-seed accuracies across the two builds and record mean time against the E036 build. (3) Keep max-autotune with cudagraphs, but pin kernel choice by persisting the inductor/autotune cache under submissions/arena/. Populate it from a synthetic-data build only, never real data. Do two fresh-process builds that read the pinned cache and compare per-seed accuracies. First check RULES.md and the submission contract to confirm that a shipped compile cache is allowed. If it is not, report arm (3) as diagnostic only. Commit only if arm (2) or arm (3) is bit-identical across rebuilds at ≤0.5% time cost versus E036. In that case it becomes the deterministic baseline, and every later idea compares seeds 0–2 and 13–32 against it exactly.
ideas.expected: (1) Bit-identical, about 85% likely. (2) Bit-identical across rebuilds, about 70% likely, at +0.3 to +1.0% time (E015's cudagraph gain was −0.9%). (3) Bit-identical with about 0% time change, if the cache is allowed. Accuracy is unchanged in distribution, but the 3-seed mean lands at one fixed value, about 0.750–0.754. If (1) fails, nondeterministic kernels cause the spread, pinning cannot help, and every comparison must stay at 20 seeds per arm. Time objective: change between −0.2% and +1%, so this is not expected to produce a new best by itself.

ideas.description: Explore/exploit: remove the last full-resolution tensor from the stem. E047 measured g1.conv1 (24→128 at 31×31) at about 0.45× group-2 efficiency, and the 128-channel 31×31 activation feeding the max-pool is the largest memory-bound tensor in the net. E043/E028 showed the stem's 31×31 work costs far more than its FLOP share. On the E036 tip, replace group 1's 'conv1 (3×3, pad 1) → 2×2 max-pool' with a single 3×3 conv with stride 2 and padding 0 (31→15, the same 15×15 output as now, so groups 2/3 and their map sizes 15/7/3 are unchanged at 32 px). At 28/24/20 px it gives 13/11/9, which also matches the current pool outputs; verify this for each resolution in code. Keep the same channel counts, BN-GELU after it, init scheme and RNG draw order (same weight shape). The whitening detach (20%) and group-1 freeze (75%) stay unchanged. Recapture every resolution and variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E036 baseline, plus seeds 0–2. Record the per-step time at 32 px (full and frozen) for the H6 accounting.
ideas.expected: conv1 FLOPs fall about 4×, and the 128×31×31 write/read and pool backward disappear. Expect about −3 to −5 ms per unfrozen 32 px step and −1.5 to −2.5 ms per frozen step, proportionally less at low resolution. Total time −5 to −9% (about 4.85–5.05 s). 20-seed mean −0.6 to 0 pp, median −0.25: learned strided downsampling loses max-pool's local translation invariance. It beats the epoch dial (~1.5 s/pp) if the loss is ≤0.25 pp for ≥0.35 s. That would make it the base for an epoch top-up that nets a feasible time below E036. A loss ≥0.4 pp means the stem needs full-resolution conv features and closes the stem-structure branch of H2.5.

ideas.description: Exploit, combining two near-misses. Conditional: run only after I075 reports. Base: I075's recipe (group-2 freeze plus a +0.25 epoch top-up) if its 20-seed mean is within 0.03 pp of same-build E036 or above it; otherwise E036. Add E048's loss-based selection exactly as committed in 4ffd290: per-sample losses from the compiled step are scattered into a GPU buffer reset in prepare, and from epoch 2 on each epoch shuffles only the 95% highest-loss samples, with the ragged batch dropped. Also add a further +0.25 true epoch, so the net step count falls by only about 5 steps rather than E048's 11. Resolution, LR triangle, Lookahead, whitening detach and freeze points all stay as fractions of the new step count. Capture the modified variants in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against the base and E036 in the same build session, plus seeds 0–2. This answers W3's crux in its stackable form: does selection beat the dial once the dial's top-up pays for it?
ideas.expected: Time −2 to −3.5% vs the base (about 0.10–0.18 s; on I075's base that is about 5.05–5.1 s, below E036's 5.31). 20-seed mean −0.15 to +0.05 pp vs the base, median −0.05. Selection's measured rate (E048 ~1.85 s/pp) should slightly beat the top-up. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥0.753 and the 20-seed mean ≥0.7545 (or within 0.03 pp of the same-build E036). A loss ≥0.12 pp vs the base means selection is no better than the dial once paid for, which closes H2.7.

ideas.description: Exploit, freeze-dose extension of the cascade (W6's crux). Conditional: run only if I075 keeps, i.e. the group-2 freeze plus top-up is within 0.03 pp of same-build E036 at ≥2% less time. On I075's recipe, move the group-2 freeze start from 90% to 85% of steps, with the group-2 LR annealed from 70% (the 32 px switch) to 0 by 85%. The frozen-group-2 32 px variant then covers the last 15% (about 36 steps instead of 23). Nothing else changes, including the step count, group-1 freeze at 75%, whitening detach, Lookahead and resolution. The variant already exists, so no new shapes are needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against I075's recipe and E036 in the same build session, plus seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time about −0.12 to −0.15 s more (13 steps × about 10 ms saved per E046), about −2.5% vs I075's recipe, to about 4.95–5.05 s. 20-seed mean −0.25 to 0 pp vs I075's recipe, median −0.08. Supports a longer cascade if the loss is ≤0.08 pp (rate ≥1.5 s/pp). A loss ≥0.15 pp means group 2 must keep learning through the first part of the 32 px averaging window, which caps the cascade at 10%.

structured_output.summary:
The loop now has two limits: noise and margin. Every recent cut (E042, E045, E046, E048) landed between its thresholds. The tip's seeds 0–2 mean ranged from 0.7497 to 0.7544 across four builds of the same commit, and the systems branch is essentially closed (E047: 2.8% GPU idle, convs at 200–270 TFLOP/s). Boosters on their own cannot win, because they add time and the committee vetoes them. So every new idea is either a time cut with a plausible rate better than the epoch dial, or a test that reduces noise.

The queue keeps I076 (non-step copies; 3/4 improve votes), I078 (ReLU; it settles W6's bytes-bound crux; 0 harm votes) and I075 (running). Four ideas are added:
- **H4.1.5 determinism test (explore, priority 3):** no-cudagraph builds versus a pinned autotune cache. If either is bit-identical across rebuilds at ≤0.5% cost, the build lottery disappears from every later comparison.
- **H2.5 strided stem conv (priority 3):** replace g1.conv1 plus max-pool with a 3×3 stride-2 pad-0 conv. This removes the last full-resolution 128-channel tensor while keeping the 15/7/3 maps. It is the one large untested structural cut, about −5 to −9% time, and is worth keeping if it costs ≤0.25 pp.
- **H2.7.1 (priority 3, conditional on I075):** stack E048's selection plus a +0.25 epoch top-up on I075's recipe.
- **H2.6.8 (priority 2, conditional on I075):** extend the group-2 freeze to the last 15%, testing W6's dose crux.

Nothing is dropped. No queued idea's hypothesis is settled, and none has majority harm votes. One note for the tree: W5 reports that Muon renormalizes the filters and applies no wd. If the code confirms this, H1.5.4 is settled without a run, and all wd results are really SGD-group (BN-bias/head) results.
